title: Payroll tax calculation: how gross pay becomes net pay | Omnia.tax
description: How payroll tax is calculated, step by step: FICA wage base ($184,500 in 2026), federal and state withholding, unemployment tax, a worked example.
h1: Payroll tax calculation, step by step

faq.q: How do you calculate payroll taxes?
faq.a: Start with gross pay, subtract the deductions that are pre-tax for each tax, then apply each tax to its own taxable wages: Social Security at 6.2% up to the wage base, Medicare at 1.45%, federal income tax from the employee's Form W-4, then state and local tax. Employers add federal and state unemployment tax on top.

faq.q: What is the Social Security wage base?
faq.a: $184,500 for 2026 and $192,300 for 2027. Social Security tax stops once an employee's wages for the year pass that amount; Medicare has no cap.

faq.q: Is a 401(k) deferral subject to payroll tax?
faq.a: It depends on the tax. A traditional 401(k) deferral reduces federal and most state income tax wages, but it is still subject to Social Security and Medicare. That difference between taxes is the most common cause of payroll tax errors.

faq.q: Can an API calculate payroll taxes for me?
faq.a: Yes. Omnia.tax takes earnings, deductions, a Form W-4, year-to-date wages and the work location, and returns each tax line with the wages it applied to and who pays it. It calculates; you still file and deposit.

faq.q: What is a payroll tax calculation engine?
faq.a: Software that takes one paycheck's earnings, deductions, withholding certificates and location and returns each payroll tax with the wages it applied to and who pays it. It calculates; it does not file, deposit or pay.

faq.q: What is the difference between a payroll tax engine and payroll software?
faq.a: Payroll software runs payroll: employees, pay runs, employee payments, filings. A tax engine is one component inside it, responsible only for the tax math. Many payroll products embed an engine rather than build the rules themselves.

faq.q: Does a payroll tax engine file my taxes?
faq.a: No. Omnia.tax calculates withholding and employer taxes. You, or your payroll provider, still file returns and deposit the tax.

title: Income tax calculation engine for payroll withholding | Omnia.tax

h1: Income tax calculation engine for payroll

faq.q: What is an income tax calculation engine?
faq.a: A component that works out how much income tax to withhold from each paycheck, using the employee's withholding certificates and the federal, state and local rules for the check date.

faq.q: Is withholding the same as the tax an employee owes?
faq.a: No. Withholding is an estimate collected through the year from the employee's W-4 and pay. The employee's actual tax is settled on their return, so a refund or a balance due is normal.

faq.q: How does federal withholding use the Form W-4?
faq.a: The engine annualises the wages, adjusts for filing status and the W-4 entries (multiple jobs, dependents, other income, deductions), finds the bracket, then divides back to one paycheck and adds any extra withholding.

faq.q: Does it support the current Form W-4?
faq.a: Yes. It implements the 2020-or-later Form W-4: filing status, the multiple-jobs checkbox, the dependent credit, other income, deductions and extra withholding.

faq.q: Are amounts in dollars or cents?
faq.a: Integer cents everywhere, in requests and responses. A request that sends dollars with a decimal is rejected with a field-level error.

faq.q: How do I calculate net pay from gross pay?
faq.a: Subtract pre-tax deductions, work out each tax on its own taxable wages, then subtract the employee taxes and the post-tax deductions from gross. The API does this in one call and returns each step.

faq.q: What does gross to net mean in payroll?
faq.a: It is the calculation from an employee's gross pay to their net pay: subtract pre-tax deductions, the taxes withheld from the employee and any post-tax deductions.

faq.q: Are employer taxes part of net pay?
faq.a: No. Employer taxes such as the employer share of Social Security and Medicare and unemployment tax are an extra cost to the employer. They do not reduce the employee's net pay.

faq.q: What is a payroll gross-up?
faq.a: Paying an employee enough gross that the amount they take home after tax equals an agreed figure, common for after-tax bonuses and relocation payments.

faq.q: Is the gross-up answer exact?

description: How federal income tax withholding is calculated from the Form W-4 percentage method, with a worked paycheck run through the engine and each step explained.

faq.q: How is federal income tax withholding calculated?
faq.a: From the Form W-4 using the IRS percentage method: annualise the check, adjust for filing status and the W-4 entries, find the bracket, subtract credits, then divide back to one paycheck and add any extra withholding.

faq.q: What does the multiple-jobs checkbox do?
faq.a: It selects the higher-withholding table, because each job is withheld as if it were the only one. It is on the Form W-4 as step 2.

faq.q: Does this cover pensions?
faq.a: Pension and annuity payments are withheld by a different method: Form W-4P and Pub 15-T Worksheet 1B for periodic payments, and Form W-4R for lump sums and rollovers. Omnia.tax calculates federal withholding on them in a separate pension request, and does not calculate state withholding on them.

title: Bonus tax withholding calculation: supplemental wages | Omnia.tax
description: How bonus withholding is calculated: the flat 22% supplemental rate or aggregating with regular pay. A worked $5,000 bonus run through the engine, line by line.

faq.q: How is a bonus taxed?
faq.a: Federal withholding on a bonus can use a flat supplemental rate (22% for most amounts) instead of the regular percentage method. Social Security and Medicare apply as normal, and each state has its own treatment.

faq.q: Why is tax on my bonus so high?
faq.a: The flat withholding rate can exceed your normal marginal rate, so more is withheld from that check than will be owed. The difference is settled when you file.

faq.q: Can an employer withhold a bonus at the regular rate?
faq.a: Yes. Aggregating the bonus with regular pay and running the normal method is the alternative to the flat rate. The engine aggregates by default for states where the flat rate is an employer option.

title: Pre-tax deductions: which taxes they reduce | Omnia.tax

h1: Pre-tax deductions and which taxes they reduce

faq.q: Does a 401(k) contribution reduce Social Security tax?
faq.a: No. A traditional 401(k) deferral reduces federal and most state income tax wages but is still subject to Social Security and Medicare.

faq.q: Does a health insurance premium reduce payroll taxes?
faq.a: A premium paid through a section 125 cafeteria plan reduces federal income tax, Social Security and Medicare wages, and most state income tax wages.

faq.q: Do all states treat pre-tax deductions the same way?
faq.a: No. States differ on 401(k) deferrals, HSA contributions and others, so the treatment is set per state and per deduction category.

title: FICA tax calculation: Social Security and Medicare | Omnia.tax
description: FICA calculation for 2026: Social Security 6.2% up to $184,500, Medicare 1.45% with no cap, and Additional Medicare. A worked example at the cap.

faq.q: What is the Social Security wage base for 2026?
faq.a: $184,500. It is $192,300 for 2027. Social Security tax stops once an employee's wages for the year pass it.

faq.q: What is the FICA tax rate?
faq.a: Social Security is 6.2% from the employee and 6.2% from the employer; Medicare is 1.45% from each, with no cap. Employees also pay 0.9% Additional Medicare on wages above $200,000.

faq.q: Does the employer pay FICA too?
faq.a: Yes. The employer pays a matching share of Social Security and Medicare, which is a cost to the employer and not taken from the employee. The Additional Medicare Tax is paid by the employee only.

title: Paycheck calculation formula: gross to net pay | Omnia.tax
description: The paycheck calculation formula from gross pay to net pay, with the order of steps, what each tax is applied to, and a worked example from the engine.

faq.q: What is the formula for net pay?
faq.a: Net pay equals gross pay minus pre-tax deductions, minus the taxes withheld from the employee, minus post-tax deductions. Employer taxes are not part of it.

faq.q: Why is my net pay not gross minus a flat percentage?
faq.a: Each tax has its own rate, cap and taxable wages, federal income tax uses brackets, and deductions affect each tax differently. The effective rate changes with pay level and location.

title: Pension and annuity withholding calculation (Form W-4P) | Omnia.tax
description: How federal withholding on periodic pension and annuity payments is calculated from Form W-4P (Pub 15-T Worksheet 1B), with worked examples from the engine.

faq.q: How is withholding on a pension calculated?
faq.a: For periodic payments, from the payee's Form W-4P using Pub 15-T Worksheet 1B: annualise the payment, apply the standard adjustment and the form's entries, find the annual tax on the standard schedule, subtract credits, and divide by the number of payments.

faq.q: What if a retiree gave the payer no Form W-4P?
faq.a: The payer withholds as if the payee were Single with no entries in Steps 2 to 4. For payments that began before 2022 with no form, the payee is treated as married claiming three allowances, under the older rules.

faq.q: Is Social Security or Medicare tax withheld from a pension?
faq.a: No. FICA applies to wages. A pension payment has federal income tax withheld and, depending on the state, state income tax.

faq.q: Does Omnia.tax calculate state tax on pensions?
faq.a: No. It calculates federal withholding on pension, annuity and IRA payments. State and local withholding on them varies by state and is not calculated.

title: Eligible rollover and lump-sum withholding (Form W-4R) | Omnia.tax
description: How 10% and 20% withholding works for lump sums, IRA distributions and eligible rollover distributions (Form W-4R), with examples from the engine.
h1: Eligible rollover and nonperiodic payment withholding

faq.q: How much is withheld from an eligible rollover distribution?
faq.a: The payer must withhold 20% of the taxable amount unless the payment is rolled over directly. The payee can ask for a higher rate on Form W-4R but not a lower one, including zero.

faq.q: What is the default withholding on a 401(k) or IRA lump sum?
faq.a: An IRA distribution payable on demand or any other nonperiodic payment defaults to 10%, and the payee can choose 0% to 100%. A lump sum from a 401(k) that could be rolled over is an eligible rollover distribution and defaults to 20%.

faq.q: Can a payee choose no withholding?
faq.a: On a nonperiodic payment, yes, by entering 0% on Form W-4R, unless the payment is delivered outside the United States and its territories. On an eligible rollover distribution, no.

faq.q: What payroll taxes does an employer pay?
faq.a: The employer match of Social Security and Medicare, federal unemployment tax (FUTA), state unemployment tax (SUTA), and in some states paid-leave or disability contributions. A few places add quarterly payroll taxes such as New York MCTMT.

faq.q: How much extra does an employee cost in payroll tax?
faq.a: It depends on pay and state. The employer match of Social Security and Medicare is 7.65% of wages up to the Social Security cap, plus unemployment tax on the first part of the wages.

faq.q: What is the FUTA rate?
faq.a: FUTA is 6.0% of the first $7,000 of each employee's wages. Employers who pay their state unemployment tax on time normally get a credit that brings the effective rate to 0.6%.

title: FUTA and SUTA calculation: unemployment tax for employers | Omnia.tax
description: How FUTA and SUTA are calculated: $7,000 federal base, state wage bases from $7,000 to $78,200, new-employer rates and the credit.

faq.q: What is the difference between FUTA and SUTA?
faq.a: FUTA is the federal unemployment tax, 6.0% of the first $7,000 per employee before a credit. SUTA is the state unemployment tax, with a different wage base and rate in each state. Both are paid by the employer.

faq.q: How is SUTA calculated?
faq.a: The employer's assigned rate times the employee's wages up to the state wage base for the year. A new employer pays the state's new-employer rate until it has an experience-based rate.

faq.q: Do employees pay unemployment tax?
faq.a: In most states no, it is employer-paid. A few states also collect a small employee contribution for related programs, which the engine returns as its own line.

faq.q: What is nexus for payroll tax?
faq.a: A legal presence in a state, such as an office or employees there, that can require an employer to register and withhold in that state. It is a fact about the employer that the request carries, because the engine cannot determine it.
